Active Industries

Active — Core Sector
Cement

Cement is Jayveecons' founding industry — we were established in 1987 specifically to serve small-scale cement plants using Vertical Shaft Kiln technology. Nearly four decades later, cement remains our deepest area of expertise, spanning VSK systems, rotary kiln components, raw material handling, clinker conveying, and finished cement storage. We understand the full cement process chain from quarry to despatch silo.

Active
Mining, Ore
Processing &
Aggregates

Mining covers three distinct engineering challenges that Jayveecons addresses separately. Run-of-mine extraction and aggregates production demand heavy-duty conveying, primary and secondary crushing, and scalping screens that can handle large, irregular, abrasive feed. Ore processing — particularly for limestone, bauxite, iron ore, and mineral sands — adds classification, grinding, and thermal treatment steps where precise particle size control is critical. Finished aggregate handling requires high-throughput belt conveyors, elevated stockpile systems, and efficient load-out infrastructure. Jayveecons has engineered equipment for all three phases, and we understand that each has different wear rates, duty cycles, and maintenance access requirements.

Food &
Agriculture

Food processing demands handling systems that are hygienic, gentle on product, and constructed to food-safety standards. Jayveecons supplies stainless steel screw conveyors, bucket elevators, and storage systems for grain, pulses, spices, sugar, and processed food operations. All food-grade equipment is designed with full-flush cleanability, food-approved materials, and smooth internal surfaces that meet applicable hygiene codes.

Municipal solid waste, industrial process waste, and biomass streams all require robust handling before they can be processed, stored, or converted to energy. Jayveecons designs conveying and processing systems for the challenging nature of waste feedstocks — variable particle size, abrasive and corrosive constituents, and the need for enclosed, dust-controlled handling to meet environmental regulations.

Steel &

Steel and ceramic manufacturing involve high-temperature, high-abrasion material streams that demand equipment built to withstand extreme conditions. Jayveecons supplies heat-resistant conveying systems for sinter, slag, and refractory materials, as well as grinding and classification equipment for the ceramic raw material preparation. Our experience with refractory-lined structures and high-temperature sealing comes directly from our kiln engineering background.

Where We Are Growing

Equipment Ready.
Experience Transferable.

The equipment we build for cement plants, mines, and food processing operations is the same equipment these sectors need — the material characteristics differ, the engineering principles do not. If your operation in any of these sectors handles bulk solids, powders, or granular material, Jayveecons has fabricated something like it before.

Oil & Gas
Diversifying With Proven Equipment

Upstream and midstream oil and gas operations move large volumes of bulk solids — proppants (frac sand), drilling muds, barite, and bentonite in drilling; petroleum coke, catalyst fines, and sulphur in refining. These materials demand enclosed, leak-proof conveying systems and pressure-rated containment vessels built to material-specific standards.

What we bring to this sector: Enclosed screw conveyors suited to dusty and hazardous bulk solids; belt and bucket systems scaled for high-volume proppant handling at drilling sites; fabricated pressure vessels and storage systems for bulk chemical intermediates; experience with abrasion-resistant material selection from our mining work. Where API or ASME documentation is specified, we work to those requirements.
Pharmaceuticals
Diversifying With Proven Equipment

Pharmaceutical bulk handling requires precision, containment, and cleanability above all else. Active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), excipients, and formulation powders must be transferred without contamination, without cross-mixing, and with full material traceability. Equipment construction must permit clean-in-place or strip-down cleaning, with no crevices, dead zones, or surface finishes that trap product.

What we bring to this sector: Stainless steel screw conveyors and bucket elevators designed to Ra surface finish requirements; crevice-free weld geometry; contained transfer points that eliminate open-air product exposure; IBC handling systems; full material certification (mill certificates, test reports) and dimensional inspection documentation. Our food-grade fabrication experience is the direct foundation for pharma-grade work.
Agriculture Processing
Diversifying With Proven Equipment

Industrial-scale post-harvest operations — grain reception and storage, oilseed crushing, rice milling, sugar processing, and animal feed compounding — require handling systems that are high-throughput, gentle on product quality, and designed for the seasonal intensity of harvest intake. Moisture management, pest exclusion, and dust control are critical operating parameters, not afterthoughts.

What we bring to this sector: High-capacity bucket elevators and belt conveyors for grain intake and transfer; flat-bottom and hopper-bottom silos for short and long-term storage with aeration systems; rotary dryers for moisture reduction of harvested grain; screw conveyors and feeders for milling and blending operations. Our food-processing background means food-safe material selection is standard, not an upgrade.
Technical Depth

Five Sectors.
Each One Built
Different Expertise.

Broad sector coverage only becomes an asset when each sector has genuinely stretched the engineering. Ours has. Each of the five industries we serve presented a specific class of problem that our team had to solve — and those solutions are now part of how we approach every new project.

The proof points on the right are not positioning statements. They are descriptions of actual engineering constraints we have worked through, and the capability those constraints left behind.

Cement — Thermal & Process Engineering
VSK and rotary kiln systems required us to master refractory lining design, high-temperature sealing, nodulisation, and clinker discharge mechanics. That thermal engineering capability — understanding how materials behave at 900–1450°C — is not something most conveying companies possess.
Mining & Ore Processing — Abrasion & Wear Engineering
Handling hard rock, ore fines, and crusher discharge taught us to design for abrasive wear from first principles — selecting AR steel grades, hard-facing flighting, ceramic-lined chutes, and impact-rated idler spacing. That wear engineering knowledge translates directly into longer-life equipment in any abrasive duty.
Food & Agriculture — Hygienic Fabrication
Food-grade work enforced a different fabrication discipline: full-penetration welds ground flush, continuous internal fillets, smooth surface finishes, stainless 304/316 construction, and cleanability as a primary design constraint. That discipline now means we can meet hygiene standards in pharmaceutical and agri-processing work without relearning anything.
Waste Management — Containment & Corrosion Design
Municipal and industrial waste streams are chemically aggressive, variably sized, and environmentally regulated. Designing for them demanded enclosed conveying architecture, corrosion-allowance engineering, and dust-tight construction — constraints that have made our standard designs inherently more robust for any corrosive or dust-sensitive application.
Steel & Ceramics — High-Temperature Structural Engineering
Steel plant and ceramic raw material handling operates at elevated temperatures with heavy, abrasive loads. Designing chain-type bucket elevators, heat-resistant belt conveyors, and refractory-lined chutes for these conditions demanded structural and thermal analysis that most fabricators are not equipped to carry out in-house.
